the stepwise control of the differentiation process of embryonic stem cell toward hematopoiesis is extremely efficient, resulting in the generation of a very high frequency and purity of hematopoietically committed precursors.
the differentiation of embryonic cells to hematopoetic fate is driven by the sequential action of four factors, BMP4, activin, bFGF, and VEGF.
the stepwise specification of mouse ES cells toward hematopoietic lineage requires the sequential stimulation by BMP4, activinA, FGF2 and VEGF.

understanding the mechanisms that control the differentiation of embryonic and hematopoietic stem cells.

The main takeaway from our work is that
Bmp4, bFGF, activin A and VEGF are sufficient to drive mouse embryonic stem (mES) cells to hematopoetic fate.

the differentiation of ES cells to hematopoeitic fate is driven by the sequential exposure of mesoderm precursors to Bmp4 (to promote mesoderm differentiation), activin A and bFGF (to promote hemangioblast differentiation) and VEGFa (to promote the production of committed hematopoietics).
the differentiation of mouse embryonic stem (mES) cells into blood progenitors can be controlled in a stepwise fashion.
